- If sentiment is consistently neutral or negative (0.00), model tends to overestimate prices; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% for early periods.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% in next 3–5 days.
- When true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 75–80), model persists in upward trend; apply downward bias of 2–5% for 5-day horizon.
- If sentiment history includes positive signals (e.g., >0.20), model underestimates upside; increase forecast by 1–3% for next 3–7 days.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often fails to capture late-period volatility; add 1–2% upward adjustment if true outcome shows >85% of 30d is above 80.
- If model forecast is flat or rising slowly but true outcome shows sudden drop (e.g., >5% drop in 2 days), reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 5 days.
- When sentiment is positive but model is flat, assume market is “waiting” — increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
